selection_policy: Run H1 first as a measurement-harness test. H2-H4 are pre-registered follow-ons and may not be described as supported until their own isolated experiment and replication pass.

hypotheses.mechanism: When evidence is compressed to aggregate fit summaries, information that distinguishes structural and latent causes is removed; a repair policy therefore defaults to lower-level parameter adjustment.
hypotheses.executable_direction: Semi-synthetic residual cases with known measurement, parameter, structural and latent causes; compare a global-summary policy against a residual-signature policy.
hypotheses.prediction: The compressed policy has lower repair-level accuracy and a higher under-revision rate, particularly for structural and latent causes, across fixed seeds 7, 19 and 31.
hypotheses.falsifier: Compression preserves comparable repair accuracy and does not raise under-revision against the same cases and policies.
hypotheses.novelty_response: The question is not whether model criticism detects mismatch, but whether evidence granularity changes the selected level of repair under known hidden causes.
hypotheses.status: measurement-harness-complete; requires real-agent or public-data replication

hypotheses.mechanism: Residual signatures can diagnose a repair level only if policy confidence tracks its actual repair accuracy across heterogeneous cases.
hypotheses.executable_direction: Add confidence scores and perturbed signatures; measure repair-level calibration, selective risk and abstention value.
hypotheses.prediction: A policy that abstains below a calibrated confidence threshold reduces false repair commitments at a bounded coverage cost.
hypotheses.falsifier: Selective abstention does not improve risk at matched coverage, or confidence is uncorrelated with repair correctness.
hypotheses.novelty_response: Separates detection of model inadequacy from awareness of whether the proposed repair is justified.

hypotheses.mechanism: The optimal response to a residual depends jointly on expected repair accuracy, expected information gain and repair cost; always escalating to the richest representation is inefficient.
hypotheses.executable_direction: Assign predeclared costs to measurement collection, parameter recalibration, structural expansion and latent-variable measurement; compare fixed policies to a cost-aware route.
hypotheses.prediction: A cost-aware policy matches or exceeds high-cost escalation on utility while spending less on cases whose signatures support cheaper repairs.
hypotheses.falsifier: Cost-aware routing loses utility at the same budget or selects expensive repairs without accuracy benefit.
hypotheses.novelty_response: Connects model criticism to a decision policy over repair levels rather than only a goodness-of-fit score.

hypotheses.mechanism: A representation that absorbs anomalous groups into aggregate fit can look adequate in-distribution while failing to preserve the anomaly under a shifted regime.
hypotheses.executable_direction: Train repair policies on one mixture proportion and evaluate identification plus held-out prediction under shifted proportions and unseen interactions.
hypotheses.prediction: Correct-level repairs preserve anomaly recall and improve held-out-regime performance relative to aggregate-only optimization.
hypotheses.falsifier: Aggregate-only optimization matches anomaly recall and held-out performance across predeclared shifts.
hypotheses.novelty_response: Tests whether representation repair is tied to scientific anomaly preservation rather than average predictive fit alone.
